proposed.text: After a successful change of use application is approved and all conditions are met, what specific document does the Building Official issue to authorize the new occupancy?

options.text: A Certificate of Occupancy updated to reflect the new use classification
An amended Building Permit that incorporates the new use into the original permit record
A Certificate of Occupancy — a separate instrument specific to approved occupancy changes
A Zoning Compliance Certificate issued jointly by the BO and the local planning office

proposed.rationale: Under PD 1096, the specific document issued upon approval of a change of use application is the CERTIFICATE OF USE — distinct from the Certificate of Occupancy issued for new construction. The Certificate of Occupancy is the instrument that legally authorizes the new occupancy classification. While a new CO (per Sec. 309.9) is also required, the intermediate authorization document specifically issued for the change process is the Certificate of Occupancy.
proposed.explanation: Certificate of USE (change process) vs Certificate of OCCUPANCY (new construction). Both are issued by the Building Official but serve different purposes and apply to different scenarios. Confusing these two is a common exam error.
